part1.tipFr: "She is picking some flowers" (B) est tentant car des fleurs sont clairement sur la photo, mais vérifiez qui fait quoi — si c'est un homme, pas une femme, qui interagit avec elles, le sujet seul élimine B quel que soit le verbe.

part1.tipId: "She is picking some flowers" (B) menggoda karena bunga jelas ada di foto, tetapi periksa siapa yang melakukan apa — jika seorang pria, bukan wanita, yang berinteraksi dengan bunga itu, subjeknya saja sudah menyingkirkan B tanpa memandang kata kerjanya.

part1.tipTh: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof" (B) เป็นกับดักเพราะมันยืนยันการกระทำที่เสร็จสิ้นซึ่งภาพไม่สามารถยืนยันได้ว่าเกิดขึ้น — สถานะปัจจุบันที่มองเห็นได้ชัดเจน (ประตูรถปกคลุมด้วยหิมะ) ปลอดภัยกว่าการกระทำในอดีตที่อนุมานขึ้น
part1.tipZh: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof"（B）是陷阱，因為它斷言了一個照片無法驗證是否發生過的已完成動作——清楚可見的現狀（車門覆蓋著雪）比推測出的過去動作更安全。
part1.tipFr: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof" (B) est un piège car il affirme une action achevée que la photo ne peut vérifier — un état présent clairement visible (portière couverte de neige) est plus sûr qu'une action passée déduite.
part1.tipKo: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof"(B)는 사진이 확인할 수 없는 완료된 동작을 단언하기 때문에 함정입니다 — 명확하게 보이는 현재 상태(눈 덮인 차 문)가 추론된 과거 동작보다 더 안전합니다.
part1.tipJa: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof"（B）は、写真では起こったか確認できない完了した動作を断言しているため罠です — 明確に見える現在の状態（雪に覆われた車のドア）の方が、推測された過去の動作よりも安全です。
part1.tipId: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof" (B) adalah jebakan karena menegaskan tindakan selesai yang tidak dapat diverifikasi oleh foto telah terjadi — keadaan sekarang yang terlihat jelas (pintu mobil tertutup salju) lebih aman daripada tindakan masa lalu yang disimpulkan.
part1.tipEl: Το "he has already shoveled the snow off the roof" (B) είναι παγίδα επειδή βεβαιώνει μια ολοκληρωμένη ενέργεια που η φωτογραφία δεν μπορεί να επαληθεύσει ότι συνέβη — μια σαφώς ορατή τρέχουσα κατάσταση (η πόρτα του αυτοκινήτου καλυμμένη με χιόνι) είναι πιο ασφαλής από μια συναγόμενη ενέργεια του παρελθόντος.
part1.tipEs: "He has already shoveled the snow off the roof" (B) es una trampa porque afirma una acción completada que la foto no puede verificar que ocurrió — un estado presente claramente visible (puerta del auto cubierta de nieve) es más seguro que una acción pasada inferida.

part1.tip: "Full of students" (A) directly contradicts "empty" (B) — when two options are exact opposites, one of them is almost always the answer, so look at the photo specifically to judge occupancy rather than assuming a lecture hall is normally full.
part1.tipVn: "Full of students" (A) trực tiếp trái ngược với "empty" (B) — khi hai đáp án đối lập hoàn toàn, một trong hai gần như luôn là đáp án đúng, nên hãy nhìn kỹ ảnh để đánh giá mức độ đông đúc thay vì mặc định giảng đường thường đầy người.
part1.tipTh: "Full of students" (A) ขัดแย้งโดยตรงกับ "empty" (B) — เมื่อสองตัวเลือกตรงข้ามกันอย่างสิ้นเชิง หนึ่งในนั้นมักจะเป็นคำตอบเสมอ ดังนั้นให้ดูภาพเฉพาะเจาะจงเพื่อตัดสินความหนาแน่นแทนที่จะสันนิษฐานว่าห้องบรรยายมักจะเต็ม
part1.tipZh: "Full of students"（A）與 "empty"（B）直接矛盾——當兩個選項完全相反時，其中一個幾乎總是答案，因此請具體觀察照片來判斷人數多寡，而不是假設演講廳通常都是滿的。
part1.tipFr: "Full of students" (A) contredit directement "empty" (B) — quand deux options sont exactement opposées, l'une des deux est presque toujours la réponse, alors regardez spécifiquement la photo pour juger de l'occupation plutôt que de supposer qu'un amphithéâtre est normalement plein.
part1.tipKo: "Full of students"(A)는 "empty"(B)와 정반대입니다 — 두 선택지가 정확히 반대일 때는 거의 항상 둘 중 하나가 정답이므로, 강의실이 보통 꽉 차 있다고 가정하기보다 사진을 구체적으로 보고 좌석 상황을 판단하세요.
part1.tipJa: "Full of students"（A）は "empty"（B）と直接矛盾します — 二つの選択肢が正反対の場合、そのどちらかがほぼ常に正解なので、講堂が通常満員だと仮定するのではなく、写真を具体的に見て収容状況を判断しましょう。
part1.tipId: "Full of students" (A) secara langsung bertentangan dengan "empty" (B) — ketika dua pilihan benar-benar berlawanan, salah satunya hampir selalu jawabannya, jadi lihat foto secara spesifik untuk menilai keterisian, alih-alih mengasumsikan ruang kuliah biasanya penuh.
part1.tipEl: Το "full of students" (A) έρχεται σε άμεση αντίθεση με το "empty" (B) — όταν δύο επιλογές είναι ακριβώς αντίθετες, η μία από τις δύο είναι σχεδόν πάντα η απάντηση, οπότε κοιτάξτε συγκεκριμένα τη φωτογραφία για να κρίνετε την πληρότητα αντί να υποθέτετε ότι ένα αμφιθέατρο είναι συνήθως γεμάτο.
part1.tipEs: "Full of students" (A) contradice directamente a "empty" (B) — cuando dos opciones son exactamente opuestas, una de ellas casi siempre es la respuesta, así que mira específicamente la foto para juzgar la ocupación en vez de asumir que un auditorio suele estar lleno.

part1.tip: "Typing on the computer" (D) is a common near-miss for "looking at the computer" (A) — both involve the same object, but typing requires visible hand-on-keyboard action, while looking only requires the gaze; don't assume the more active verb just because it's plausible.
part1.tipVn: "Typing on the computer" (D) là bẫy gần đúng phổ biến cho "looking at the computer" (A) — cả hai đều liên quan đến cùng vật thể, nhưng typing đòi hỏi hành động tay trên bàn phím rõ ràng, còn looking chỉ cần ánh nhìn; đừng mặc định động từ chủ động hơn chỉ vì nó hợp lý.
part1.tipTh: "Typing on the computer" (D) เป็นการเกือบพลาดที่พบบ่อยสำหรับ "looking at the computer" (A) — ทั้งสองเกี่ยวข้องกับวัตถุเดียวกัน แต่ typing ต้องการการกระทำมือบนแป้นพิมพ์ที่มองเห็นได้ ในขณะที่ looking ต้องการแค่การจ้องมอง — อย่าสันนิษฐานกริยาที่กระตือรือร้นกว่าเพียงเพราะมันสมเหตุสมผล
part1.tipZh: "Typing on the computer"（D）常常和 "looking at the computer"（A）搞混——兩者涉及同一個物體，但 typing 需要看得見的手在鍵盤上動作，而 looking 只需要視線注視——不要僅因為聽起來合理，就假設是更主動的動詞。
part1.tipFr: "Typing on the computer" (D) est un piège fréquent pour "looking at the computer" (A) — les deux impliquent le même objet, mais taper exige une action visible des mains sur le clavier, tandis que regarder ne demande que le regard ; ne supposez pas le verbe plus actif juste parce qu'il est plausible.
part1.tipKo: "Typing on the computer"(D)는 "looking at the computer"(A)에 흔히 근접하는 오답입니다 — 둘 다 같은 물건과 관련되지만, typing은 키보드 위에서 손을 움직이는 것이 보여야 하고, looking은 시선만 있으면 됩니다 — 그럴듯하다고 해서 더 능동적인 동사를 가정하지 마세요.
part1.tipJa: "Typing on the computer"（D）は "looking at the computer"（A）によくある紛らわしい誤答です — どちらも同じ物に関わりますが、typing はキーボード上の手の動きが見える必要があり、looking は視線だけで十分です — もっともらしいというだけでより能動的な動詞を想定しないようにしましょう。
part1.tipId: "Typing on the computer" (D) adalah kesalahan hampir mirip yang umum untuk "looking at the computer" (A) — keduanya melibatkan objek yang sama, tetapi mengetik membutuhkan tindakan tangan yang terlihat di atas keyboard, sedangkan melihat hanya membutuhkan tatapan; jangan berasumsi kata kerja yang lebih aktif hanya karena masuk akal.
part1.tipEl: Το "typing on the computer" (D) είναι μια συχνή σχεδόν σωστή επιλογή για το "looking at the computer" (A) — και τα δύο αφορούν το ίδιο αντικείμενο, αλλά η πληκτρολόγηση απαιτεί ορατή ενέργεια χεριού στο πληκτρολόγιο, ενώ το κοίταγμα απαιτεί μόνο το βλέμμα — μην υποθέτετε το πιο ενεργητικό ρήμα απλώς επειδή είναι εύλογο.
part1.tipEs: "Typing on the computer" (D) es una casi-coincidencia frecuente de "looking at the computer" (A) — ambos implican el mismo objeto, pero escribir exige una acción visible de las manos en el teclado, mientras que mirar solo requiere la mirada; no asumas el verbo más activo solo porque es plausible.

part1.tip: "Tasting the vegetables" (D) and "holding a vegetable" (A) both involve vegetables, but tasting implies putting food to the mouth — a much more specific and less commonly depicted action than simply holding, so don't over-interpret a static grip as an eating action.
part1.tipVn: "Tasting the vegetables" (D) và "holding a vegetable" (A) đều liên quan đến rau củ, nhưng tasting ngụ ý đưa thức ăn vào miệng — một hành động cụ thể hơn nhiều và ít khi được mô tả hơn so với việc chỉ đơn giản là cầm, nên đừng diễn giải quá mức một động tác cầm tĩnh thành hành động ăn.
part1.tipTh: "Tasting the vegetables" (D) และ "holding a vegetable" (A) ต่างก็เกี่ยวข้องกับผัก แต่ tasting หมายถึงการนำอาหารเข้าปาก — เป็นการกระทำที่เฉพาะเจาะจงกว่ามากและมักไม่ถูกแสดงบ่อยเท่าการถือธรรมดา ดังนั้นอย่าตีความการจับที่นิ่งเกินเลยเป็นการกระทำการกิน
part1.tipZh: "Tasting the vegetables"（D）和 "holding a vegetable"（A）都涉及蔬菜，但 tasting 意味著把食物送進嘴裡——這是比單純拿著更具體、也較少見的動作，因此不要過度解讀靜態的拿握動作為進食行為。
part1.tipFr: "Tasting the vegetables" (D) et "holding a vegetable" (A) concernent tous deux des légumes, mais goûter implique de porter la nourriture à la bouche — une action bien plus spécifique et moins souvent représentée que simplement tenir ; ne surinterprétez pas une prise statique comme une action de manger.
part1.tipKo: "Tasting the vegetables"(D)와 "holding a vegetable"(A)는 둘 다 채소와 관련이 있지만, tasting은 음식을 입에 대는 것을 의미합니다 — 단순히 들고 있는 것보다 훨씬 구체적이고 덜 흔하게 묘사되는 동작이므로, 정적인 쥐는 동작을 먹는 동작으로 과대 해석하지 마세요.
part1.tipJa: "Tasting the vegetables"（D）と "holding a vegetable"（A）はどちらも野菜に関係しますが、tasting は食べ物を口に運ぶことを意味します — 単に持っているだけよりはるかに具体的で、あまり一般的でない動作なので、静的な握る動作を食べる動作だと過度に解釈しないようにしましょう。
part1.tipId: "Tasting the vegetables" (D) dan "holding a vegetable" (A) sama-sama melibatkan sayuran, tetapi tasting menyiratkan memasukkan makanan ke mulut — tindakan yang jauh lebih spesifik dan tidak sesering digambarkan dibandingkan sekadar memegang, jadi jangan terlalu menafsirkan genggaman statis sebagai tindakan makan.
part1.tipEl: Τόσο το "tasting the vegetables" (D) όσο και το "holding a vegetable" (A) αφορούν λαχανικά, αλλά η γεύση υπονοεί να φέρνεις το φαγητό στο στόμα — μια πολύ πιο συγκεκριμένη και λιγότερο συχνά απεικονιζόμενη ενέργεια από το να κρατάς απλώς κάτι, οπότε μην υπερερμηνεύετε ένα στατικό κράτημα ως ενέργεια φαγητού.
part1.tipEs: "Tasting the vegetables" (D) y "holding a vegetable" (A) implican ambas verduras, pero probar implica llevarse comida a la boca — una acción mucho más específica y menos representada que simplemente sostener, así que no interpretes en exceso un agarre estático como una acción de comer.

part5.tipVn: "Regarding" (B) là lựa chọn sai phổ biến vì nghe có vẻ cũng có thể giới thiệu mệnh đề liên quan đến thời gian, nhưng nó nghĩa là "về/liên quan đến" một chủ đề — "within" mới là giới từ đúng cho khung thời gian ("trong vòng hai ngày"), nên hãy khớp giới từ với đúng quan hệ (thời gian hay chủ đề).
part5.tipTh: "Regarding" (B) เป็นตัวเลือกผิดที่พบบ่อยเพราะฟังดูเหมือนสามารถแนะนำอนุประโยคเกี่ยวกับเวลาได้ด้วย แต่หมายถึง "เกี่ยวกับ" หัวข้อหนึ่ง — "within" เป็นบุพบทที่ถูกต้องสำหรับกรอบเวลา ("ภายในสองวัน") ดังนั้นจับคู่บุพบทกับความสัมพันธ์เฉพาะ (เวลา vs หัวข้อ)
part5.tipZh: "Regarding"（B）是常見的錯誤選項，因為它聽起來也像可以引出與時間相關的子句，但它的意思是「關於」某個主題——"within" 才是表示時間範圍（「兩天內」）的正確介詞，所以要將介詞與具體關係（時間 vs. 主題）配對。
part5.tipFr: "Regarding" (B) est un choix erroné courant car il semble aussi pouvoir introduire une proposition temporelle, mais il signifie "à propos de" un sujet — "within" est la bonne préposition pour un délai ("dans les deux jours"), associez donc la préposition à la relation précise (temps vs sujet).
part5.tipKo: "Regarding"(B)는 시간 관련 절을 도입할 수 있을 것처럼 들려서 흔한 오답이지만, 이는 주제에 대해 "~에 관하여"라는 뜻입니다 — "within"이 기간("이틀 이내")에 맞는 올바른 전치사이므로, 전치사를 정확한 관계(시간 대 주제)에 맞추세요.
part5.tipJa: "Regarding"（B）は時間に関する節を導入できるようにも聞こえるためよくある誤答ですが、これはある話題について「〜に関して」という意味です — "within" が期間（「2日以内」）に合う正しい前置詞なので、前置詞を正確な関係（時間か話題か）に合わせましょう。
part5.tipId: "Regarding" (B) adalah pilihan salah yang umum karena juga terdengar bisa memperkenalkan klausa terkait waktu, tetapi artinya "mengenai" suatu topik — "within" adalah preposisi yang tepat untuk kerangka waktu ("dalam dua hari"), jadi cocokkan preposisi dengan hubungan spesifiknya (waktu vs topik).
part5.tipEl: Το "regarding" (B) είναι μια συχνή λανθασμένη επιλογή επειδή ακούγεται σαν να μπορεί επίσης να εισάγει μια χρονική πρόταση, αλλά σημαίνει "σχετικά με" ένα θέμα — το "within" είναι η σωστή πρόθεση για ένα χρονικό πλαίσιο ("εντός δύο ημερών"), οπότε ταιριάξτε την πρόθεση με τη συγκεκριμένη σχέση (χρόνος έναντι θέματος).
part5.tipEs: "Regarding" (B) es una elección incorrecta común porque también suena como si pudiera introducir una cláusula temporal, pero significa "acerca de" un tema — "within" es la preposición correcta para un plazo ("dentro de dos días"), así que empareja la preposición con la relación precisa (tiempo vs. tema).

part5.tip: "Yet" (B) is tempting because it's also time-related, but it means "not yet" (negative expectation), while "ever" specifically refers to past experience up to now — the phrase "more...than it ever did" is a fixed comparative pattern worth memorizing.
part5.tipVn: "Yet" (B) hấp dẫn vì cũng liên quan đến thời gian, nhưng nó nghĩa "chưa" (kỳ vọng phủ định), trong khi "ever" chỉ cụ thể kinh nghiệm quá khứ tính đến hiện tại — cụm "more...than it ever did" là mẫu so sánh cố định đáng ghi nhớ.
part5.tipTh: "Yet" (B) น่าดึงดูดเพราะยังเกี่ยวข้องกับเวลาด้วย แต่หมายถึง "ยังไม่" (ความคาดหวังเชิงลบ) ในขณะที่ "ever" หมายถึงประสบการณ์ในอดีตจนถึงปัจจุบันโดยเฉพาะ — วลี "more...than it ever did" เป็นรูปแบบเปรียบเทียบคงที่ที่ควรจำ
part5.tipZh: "Yet"（B）很誘人，因為它也與時間有關，但它的意思是「還沒」（否定的預期），而 "ever" 特指從過去到現在的經歷——"more...than it ever did" 這個片語是值得記住的固定比較句型。
part5.tipFr: "Yet" (B) est tentant car il est aussi lié au temps, mais il signifie "pas encore" (attente négative), tandis que "ever" fait spécifiquement référence à une expérience passée jusqu'à maintenant — l'expression "more...than it ever did" est un schéma comparatif fixe à mémoriser.

part5.tip: "Who" (B) and "them" (C) are common wrong picks because they're both pronoun-like, but "who" is a relative pronoun (not a standalone subject) and "them" is an object pronoun — only "anyone" can stand alone as the subject of the main verb "must apply".

part5.tip: "Since" (D) is a trap because it also means "because", similar in feel to "regardless of", but "since" must be followed by a full clause (subject + verb), while the blank here precedes a noun phrase ("the building's age") — always check the grammar of what follows first.

part5.tipId: "Since" (D) adalah jebakan karena juga berarti "karena", terasa mirip dengan "regardless of", tetapi "since" harus diikuti oleh klausa lengkap (subjek + kata kerja), sedangkan bagian kosong di sini mendahului frasa kata benda ("the building's age") — selalu periksa tata bahasa dari apa yang mengikuti terlebih dahulu.
part5.tipEl: Το "since" (D) είναι παγίδα επειδή σημαίνει επίσης "επειδή", παρόμοιο σε αίσθηση με το "regardless of", αλλά το "since" πρέπει να ακολουθείται από πλήρη πρόταση (υποκείμενο + ρήμα), ενώ το κενό εδώ προηγείται μιας ονοματικής φράσης ("the building's age") — ελέγχετε πάντα πρώτα τη γραμματική αυτού που ακολουθεί.

part5.tip: This is a classic time-clause pattern: main clause uses future tense ("will V"), but the "when" clause must stay in simple present, not future — a common mistake is putting "will" in both clauses when only one should have it.
part5.tipVn: Đây là mẫu mệnh đề thời gian kinh điển: mệnh đề chính dùng thì tương lai ("will V"), nhưng mệnh đề "when" phải giữ ở hiện tại đơn, không phải tương lai — lỗi phổ biến là đặt "will" ở cả hai mệnh đề trong khi chỉ một mệnh đề nên có.
part5.tipTh: นี่คือรูปแบบอนุประโยคเวลาคลาสสิก: อนุประโยคหลักใช้ future tense ("will V") แต่อนุประโยค "when" ต้องอยู่ในปัจจุบันธรรมดา ไม่ใช่อนาคต — ความผิดพลาดทั่วไปคือใส่ "will" ในทั้งสองอนุประโยคเมื่อควรมีเพียงอันเดียว
part5.tipZh: 這是經典的時間子句模式：主要子句使用未來式（"will V"），但 "when" 子句必須保持在現在簡單式，而非未來式——常見的失誤是在兩個子句中都放上 "will"，實際上只有一個子句應該有它。
part5.tipFr: C'est le schéma classique de la proposition temporelle : la proposition principale utilise le futur ("will V"), mais la proposition en "when" doit rester au présent simple, pas au futur — une erreur courante est de mettre "will" dans les deux propositions alors qu'une seule devrait l'avoir.
part5.tipKo: 이것은 전형적인 시간절 패턴입니다: 주절은 미래시제("will V")를 사용하지만, "when"절은 미래가 아니라 단순현재를 유지해야 합니다 — 흔한 실수는 하나의 절에만 있어야 할 "will"을 두 절 모두에 넣는 것입니다.
part5.tipJa: これは典型的な時の副詞節パターンです：主節は未来形（"will V"）を使いますが、"when" 節は未来形ではなく単純現在のままでなければなりません — よくある間違いは、片方の節にだけあるべき "will" を両方の節に入れてしまうことです。
part5.tipId: Ini adalah pola klausa waktu klasik: klausa utama menggunakan bentuk masa depan ("will V"), tetapi klausa "when" harus tetap dalam present simple, bukan masa depan — kesalahan umum adalah menempatkan "will" di kedua klausa padahal hanya satu yang seharusnya memilikinya.
part5.tipEl: Αυτό είναι το κλασικό μοτίβο χρονικής πρότασης: η κύρια πρόταση χρησιμοποιεί μέλλοντα χρόνο ("will V"), αλλά η πρόταση με το "when" πρέπει να παραμείνει σε απλό ενεστώτα, όχι μέλλοντα — ένα συνηθισμένο λάθος είναι να βάζετε "will" και στις δύο προτάσεις ενώ μόνο μία θα έπρεπε να το έχει.
part5.tipEs: Este es el patrón clásico de cláusula temporal: la cláusula principal usa futuro ("will V"), pero la cláusula con "when" debe permanecer en presente simple, no en futuro — un error común es poner "will" en ambas cláusulas cuando solo una debería tenerlo.

part5.tipId: "Stunned" (D, past participle berarti terkejut/tercengang, menggambarkan orang) mudah tertukar dengan "stunning" (C, berarti sangat memukau, menggambarkan sesuatu) — pemandangan bisa "stunning" tetapi tidak pernah "stunned"; cocokkan akhiran -ing/-ed dengan apakah kata bendanya orang atau benda.
part5.tipEl: Το "stunned" (D, μετοχή παρελθόντα χρόνου που σημαίνει σοκαρισμένος/έκπληκτος, περιγράφοντας ένα άτομο) συγχέεται εύκολα με το "stunning" (C, που σημαίνει εκπληκτικά όμορφο, περιγράφοντας ένα πράγμα) — μια θέα μπορεί να είναι "stunning" αλλά ποτέ "stunned" — ταιριάξτε τις καταλήξεις -ing/-ed ανάλογα με το αν το ουσιαστικό είναι άτομο ή πράγμα.
part5.tipEs: "Stunned" (D, participio pasado que significa impactado/sorprendido, describiendo a una persona) se confunde fácilmente con "stunning" (C, que significa impresionante, describiendo una cosa) — una vista puede ser "stunning" pero nunca "stunned"; empareja las terminaciones -ing/-ed según si el sustantivo es una persona o una cosa.

part5.tip: "Extent", "awareness", and "proposal" (A, C, D) are all abstract nouns that sound business-appropriate, but only "confirmation" fits the specific meaning of a notice sent after a purchase — always check meaning fit, not just whether the noun sounds formal enough.

part5.tipTh: "Extent", "awareness" และ "proposal" (A, C, D) ล้วนเป็นคำนามนามธรรมที่ฟังดูเหมาะกับธุรกิจ แต่มีเพียง "confirmation" เท่านั้นที่ตรงกับความหมายเฉพาะของประกาศที่ถูกส่งหลังการซื้อ — ตรวจสอบความเข้ากันของความหมายเสมอ ไม่ใช่แค่ว่าคำนามฟังดูเป็นทางการพอหรือไม่
part5.tipZh: "Extent"、"awareness"、"proposal"（A、C、D）都是聽起來符合商業語境的抽象名詞，但只有 "confirmation" 符合購買後發送通知的特定含義——務必檢查語意是否契合，而不只是名詞聽起來是否夠正式。
part5.tipFr: "Extent", "awareness" et "proposal" (A, C, D) sont tous des noms abstraits qui sonnent professionnellement appropriés, mais seul "confirmation" correspond au sens précis d'un avis envoyé après un achat — vérifiez toujours l'adéquation du sens, pas seulement si le nom sonne assez formel.
part5.tipKo: "Extent", "awareness", "proposal"(A, C, D)는 모두 비즈니스에 적합하게 들리는 추상명사이지만, 구매 후 발송되는 통지라는 특정 의미에 맞는 것은 "confirmation"뿐입니다 — 명사가 충분히 격식 있게 들리는지가 아니라 항상 의미가 맞는지를 확인하세요.
part5.tipJa: "Extent"、"awareness"、"proposal"（A、C、D）はどれもビジネスに適切に聞こえる抽象名詞ですが、購入後に送られる通知という特定の意味に合うのは "confirmation" だけです — 名詞が十分にフォーマルに聞こえるかどうかではなく、常に意味の適合性を確認しましょう。
part5.tipId: "Extent", "awareness", dan "proposal" (A, C, D) semuanya kata benda abstrak yang terdengar cocok untuk bisnis, tetapi hanya "confirmation" yang cocok dengan makna spesifik dari pemberitahuan yang dikirim setelah pembelian — selalu periksa kecocokan makna, bukan hanya apakah kata bendanya terdengar cukup formal.
part5.tipEl: Τα "extent", "awareness" και "proposal" (A, C, D) είναι όλα αφηρημένα ουσιαστικά που ακούγονται κατάλληλα για επιχειρήσεις, αλλά μόνο το "confirmation" ταιριάζει με τη συγκεκριμένη σημασία μιας ειδοποίησης που στέλνεται μετά από μια αγορά — ελέγχετε πάντα την καταλληλότητα του νοήματος, όχι μόνο αν το ουσιαστικό ακούγεται αρκετά επίσημο.
part5.tipEs: "Extent", "awareness" y "proposal" (A, C, D) son todos sustantivos abstractos que suenan apropiados para negocios, pero solo "confirmation" coincide con el significado preciso de un aviso enviado después de una compra — verifica siempre la adecuación del significado, no solo si el sustantivo suena suficientemente formal.

part5.tipKo: "Corrections"(A, 명사)와 "correct"(C, 형용사)는 정답과 어근을 공유하기 때문에 유혹적이지만, 동사 "identified"를 수식하는 빈칸은 부사 "correctly"가 필요합니다 — 빈칸이 실제로 어떤 단어를 수식하는지 항상 확인하세요.

part5.tip: "Convinced" and "cautioned" (A, D) are near-miss verbs about influencing someone, but the sentence specifically needs "accompanied" (going along with someone) to match the meaning of a hearing-impaired person being assisted by an expert — test the exact real-world scenario the sentence describes.
part5.tipVn: "Convinced" và "cautioned" (A, D) là các động từ gần đúng về việc tác động đến ai đó, nhưng câu cần cụ thể "accompanied" (đi cùng ai đó) để khớp với nghĩa một người khiếm thính được một chuyên gia hỗ trợ — hãy kiểm tra đúng tình huống thực tế mà câu mô tả.
part5.tipTh: "Convinced" และ "cautioned" (A, D) เป็นกริยาที่เกือบใกล้เคียงเกี่ยวกับการมีอิทธิพลต่อใครบางคน แต่ประโยคต้องการ "accompanied" โดยเฉพาะ (ไปพร้อมกับใครบางคน) เพื่อให้ตรงกับความหมายของคนบกพร่องทางการได้ยินที่ได้รับความช่วยเหลือจากผู้เชี่ยวชาญ — ทดสอบสถานการณ์จริงที่แน่นอนที่ประโยคอธิบาย

part5.tipKo: "Convinced"와 "cautioned"(A, D)는 누군가에게 영향을 미치는 것에 관한 근접 동사이지만, 문장은 청각 장애가 있는 사람이 전문가의 도움을 받는다는 의미에 맞도록 구체적으로 "accompanied"(누군가와 동행하다)가 필요합니다 — 문장이 묘사하는 정확한 현실적 시나리오를 테스트하세요.
part5.tipJa: "Convinced" と "cautioned"（A、D）は誰かに影響を与えることに関する紛らわしい動詞ですが、文は聴覚障害のある人が専門家の助けを受けるという意味に一致させるために、具体的に "accompanied"（誰かと同行する）を必要としています — 文が説明する正確な現実のシナリオをテストしましょう。

part5.tip: The preposition "of" right after the blank is the giveaway that a noun is needed here — "appraisal" (assessment) fits, so whenever you see a preposition immediately following a blank, strongly favor a noun over a verb form.
part5.tipVn: Giới từ "of" ngay sau chỗ trống là dấu hiệu cho biết cần một danh từ ở đây — "appraisal" (đánh giá) phù hợp, nên bất cứ khi nào thấy giới từ ngay sau chỗ trống, hãy ưu tiên mạnh danh từ hơn dạng động từ.
part5.tipTh: บุพบท "of" ทันทีหลังช่องว่างเป็นตัวบ่งชี้ว่าต้องการคำนามที่นี่ — "appraisal" (การประเมิน) เหมาะสม ดังนั้นเมื่อใดก็ตามที่คุณเห็นบุพบทตามหลังช่องว่างทันที ให้เลือกคำนามมากกว่ารูปกริยาอย่างมาก
part5.tipZh: 空格後緊接的介詞 "of" 是這裡需要名詞的明顯提示——"appraisal"（評估）符合，因此每當你看到介詞緊跟在空格之後，就要強烈傾向選擇名詞而非動詞形式。

part5.tipId: Preposisi "of" tepat setelah bagian kosong ini adalah petunjuk bahwa dibutuhkan kata benda di sini — "appraisal" (penilaian) cocok, jadi kapan pun Anda melihat preposisi langsung mengikuti bagian kosong, sangat utamakan kata benda daripada bentuk kata kerja.

part5.tipEs: La preposición "of" justo después de este espacio es la pista reveladora de que aquí se necesita un sustantivo — "appraisal" (evaluación) encaja, así que cada vez que veas una preposición seguir inmediatamente a un espacio, favorece fuertemente un sustantivo sobre una forma verbal.

part5.tipFr: "Despite" et "past" (B, D) sont tentants car ce sont aussi des prépositions courantes, mais seul "except" correspond au sens "tout est inclus sauf l'eau bouillante" — cela teste le sens précis parmi plusieurs prépositions grammaticalement valides, pas seulement la grammaire.
part5.tipKo: "Despite"와 "past"(B, D)도 흔한 전치사이기 때문에 유혹적이지만, "끓는 물을 제외한 모든 것이 포함되어 있다"는 의미에 맞는 것은 "except"뿐입니다 — 이는 문법적으로 유효한 여러 전치사 중에서 정확한 의미를 시험하는 것이지, 단순히 문법만을 시험하는 것이 아닙니다.
part5.tipJa: "Despite" と "past"（B、D）も一般的な前置詞であるため魅力的ですが、「沸騰したお湯を除いてすべてが含まれる」という意味に合うのは "except" だけです — これは文法的に有効な複数の前置詞の中から正確な意味を試すものであり、単なる文法だけではありません。
part5.tipId: "Despite" dan "past" (B, D) menggoda karena juga merupakan preposisi umum, tetapi hanya "except" yang cocok dengan makna "semuanya termasuk kecuali air mendidih" — ini menguji makna yang tepat di antara beberapa preposisi yang secara gramatikal valid, bukan hanya tata bahasa.
part5.tipEl: Το "despite" και το "past" (B, D) είναι δελεαστικά επειδή είναι επίσης συνηθισμένες προθέσεις, αλλά μόνο το "except" ταιριάζει με τη σημασία "όλα περιλαμβάνονται εκτός από το βραστό νερό" — αυτό ελέγχει την ακριβή σημασία ανάμεσα σε αρκετές γραμματικά έγκυρες προθέσεις, όχι μόνο τη γραμματική.
part5.tipEs: "Despite" y "past" (B, D) son tentadores porque también son preposiciones comunes, pero solo "except" encaja con el significado "todo está incluido excepto el agua hirviendo" — esto pone a prueba el significado preciso entre varias preposiciones gramaticalmente válidas, no solo la gramática.

part5.tip: "So that" is a fixed purpose conjunction always paired with "can/could" in the following clause — memorize this whole pattern as a unit rather than treating "so" and "that" as separate, analyzable words.
part5.tipVn: "So that" là liên từ chỉ mục đích cố định, luôn đi kèm với "can/could" trong mệnh đề theo sau — hãy ghi nhớ toàn bộ mẫu này như một khối thay vì phân tích "so" và "that" như hai từ riêng biệt.
part5.tipTh: "So that" เป็นคำเชื่อมจุดประสงค์คงที่ที่จับคู่กับ "can/could" ในอนุประโยคที่ตามมาเสมอ — จำรูปแบบทั้งหมดนี้เป็นหน่วยเดียวแทนที่จะปฏิบัติต่อ "so" และ "that" เป็นคำแยกที่วิเคราะห์ได้
part5.tipZh: "So that" 是固定的目的連接詞，總是與後面子句中的 "can/could" 搭配——請把整個模式當作一個整體記住，而不是把 "so" 和 "that" 當成可以分開分析的獨立詞語。
part5.tipFr: "So that" est une conjonction de but fixe toujours associée à "can/could" dans la proposition suivante — mémorisez tout ce schéma comme une unité plutôt que de traiter "so" et "that" comme des mots séparés analysables.
part5.tipKo: "So that"는 항상 뒤따르는 절에서 "can/could"와 짝을 이루는 고정된 목적 접속사입니다 — "so"와 "that"을 분리하여 분석 가능한 단어로 취급하지 말고 이 전체 패턴을 하나의 단위로 외우세요.
part5.tipJa: "So that" は常に後続の節で "can/could" と組み合わされる固定の目的を表す接続詞です — "so" と "that" を別々に分析できる単語として扱うのではなく、このパターン全体を一つの単位として覚えましょう。
part5.tipId: "So that" adalah konjungsi tujuan tetap yang selalu dipasangkan dengan "can/could" dalam klausa berikutnya — hafalkan seluruh pola ini sebagai satu kesatuan daripada memperlakukan "so" dan "that" sebagai kata terpisah yang bisa dianalisis.
part5.tipEl: Το "so that" είναι ένας σταθερός σύνδεσμος σκοπού που συνδυάζεται πάντα με το "can/could" στην επόμενη πρόταση — αποστηθίστε ολόκληρο αυτό το μοτίβο ως ενιαία μονάδα αντί να αντιμετωπίζετε το "so" και το "that" ως ξεχωριστές, αναλύσιμες λέξεις.
part5.tipEs: "So that" es una conjunción de propósito fija siempre emparejada con "can/could" en la cláusula siguiente — memoriza todo este patrón como una unidad en vez de tratar "so" y "that" como palabras separadas y analizables.

part5.tip: "Than" and "unless" (B, C) are tempting connectors, but the sentence needs "thereby" (meaning "as a result of this") to link an action (using a side street) with its consequence (avoiding traffic) — look for a cause-effect relationship, not comparison or condition.
part5.tipVn: "Than" và "unless" (B, C) là liên từ hấp dẫn, nhưng câu cần "thereby" (nghĩa "do đó, nhờ vậy") để nối một hành động (dùng đường nhỏ) với hệ quả của nó (tránh được kẹt xe) — hãy tìm quan hệ nhân-quả, không phải so sánh hay điều kiện.
part5.tipTh: "Than" และ "unless" (B, C) เป็นคำเชื่อมที่ล่อใจ แต่ประโยคต้องการ "thereby" (หมายถึง "เป็นผลจากสิ่งนี้") เพื่อเชื่อมการกระทำ (การใช้ถนนเล็ก) กับผลลัพธ์ของมัน (การหลีกเลี่ยงการจราจร) — มองหาความสัมพันธ์เหตุ-ผล ไม่ใช่การเปรียบเทียบหรือเงื่อนไข
part5.tipZh: "Than" 和 "unless"（B、C）是誘人的連接詞，但句子需要 "thereby"（意思是「因此」）來連接一個動作（使用小路）與其結果（避開交通）——請尋找因果關係，而不是比較或條件。
part5.tipFr: "Than" et "unless" (B, C) sont des connecteurs tentants, mais la phrase a besoin de "thereby" (signifiant "grâce à cela") pour relier une action (emprunter une petite rue) à sa conséquence (éviter le trafic) — cherchez une relation de cause à effet, pas une comparaison ou une condition.
part5.tipKo: "Than"과 "unless"(B, C)는 유혹적인 연결어이지만, 문장은 어떤 행동(옆길 이용)을 그 결과(교통 정체 회피)와 연결하기 위해 "thereby"("그 결과로"라는 뜻)가 필요합니다 — 비교나 조건이 아니라 원인-결과 관계를 찾으세요.
part5.tipJa: "Than" と "unless"（B、C）は魅力的な接続語ですが、文はある行動（裏道を使う）とその結果（渋滞を避ける）を結びつけるために "thereby"（「その結果として」という意味）を必要とします — 比較や条件ではなく、因果関係を探しましょう。
part5.tipId: "Than" dan "unless" (B, C) adalah konektor yang menggoda, tetapi kalimat membutuhkan "thereby" (berarti "sebagai akibatnya") untuk menghubungkan suatu tindakan (menggunakan jalan samping) dengan konsekuensinya (menghindari lalu lintas) — cari hubungan sebab-akibat, bukan perbandingan atau syarat.
part5.tipEl: Το "than" και το "unless" (B, C) είναι δελεαστικοί σύνδεσμοι, αλλά η πρόταση χρειάζεται το "thereby" (που σημαίνει "ως αποτέλεσμα αυτού") για να συνδέσει μια ενέργεια (χρήση ενός πάροδου δρόμου) με τη συνέπειά της (αποφυγή κίνησης) — αναζητήστε μια σχέση αιτίας-αποτελέσματος, όχι σύγκριση ή προϋπόθεση.
part5.tipEs: "Than" y "unless" (B, C) son conectores tentadores, pero la oración necesita "thereby" (que significa "como resultado de esto") para vincular una acción (usar una calle lateral) con su consecuencia (evitar el tráfico) — busca una relación causa-efecto, no comparación o condición.

part5.tip: This is the fixed future-perfect time pattern: "will have + past participle" + "by the time" + present tense clause — a common mistake is using future tense in the "by the time" clause too, when it must stay present.
part5.tipVn: Đây là mẫu thì tương lai hoàn thành cố định: "will have + quá khứ phân từ" + "by the time" + mệnh đề thì hiện tại — lỗi phổ biến là dùng cả thì tương lai trong mệnh đề "by the time", trong khi nó phải giữ ở hiện tại.
part5.tipTh: นี่คือรูปแบบเวลา future perfect คงที่: "will have + past participle" + "by the time" + อนุประโยคปัจจุบัน — ความผิดพลาดทั่วไปคือใช้อนาคตในอนุประโยค "by the time" ด้วย ในขณะที่มันต้องคงอยู่ในปัจจุบัน
part5.tipZh: 這是固定的未來完成式時態模式："will have + 過去分詞" + "by the time" + 現在式子句——常見的失誤是也在 "by the time" 子句中使用未來式，而它必須保持現在式。
part5.tipFr: C'est le schéma temporel fixe du futur antérieur : "will have + participe passé" + "by the time" + proposition au présent — une erreur courante est d'utiliser aussi le futur dans la proposition "by the time", alors qu'elle doit rester au présent.
part5.tipKo: 이것은 고정된 미래완료 시간 패턴입니다: "will have + 과거분사" + "by the time" + 현재시제절 — 흔한 실수는 "by the time" 절에도 미래시제를 사용하는 것인데, 그 절은 현재시제여야 합니다.
part5.tipJa: これは固定された未来完了の時制パターンです：「will have + 過去分詞」+「by the time」+ 現在形の節 — よくある間違いは、"by the time" 節でも未来形を使ってしまうことですが、それは現在形のままでなければなりません。
part5.tipId: Ini adalah pola waktu future perfect yang tetap: "will have + past participle" + "by the time" + klausa present tense — kesalahan umum adalah menggunakan bentuk masa depan juga dalam klausa "by the time", padahal itu harus tetap present.
part5.tipEl: Αυτό είναι το σταθερό χρονικό μοτίβο του συντελεσμένου μέλλοντα: "will have + μετοχή παρελθόντα χρόνου" + "by the time" + πρόταση σε ενεστώτα — ένα συνηθισμένο λάθος είναι να χρησιμοποιείται μέλλοντας και στην πρόταση "by the time", ενώ πρέπει να παραμείνει σε ενεστώτα.
part5.tipEs: Este es el patrón temporal fijo del futuro perfecto: "will have + participio pasado" + "by the time" + cláusula en presente — un error común es usar también el futuro en la cláusula "by the time", cuando debe permanecer en presente.

part7.description:
Northshore Financial News

June 29-A local mainstay at Northshore City may soon go nationnaal. - [1] - The Northshore Creamery first opened its doors in 1951 by owner Bill Bradley and has become an iconic landmark of the city with it's huge rotating ice cream cone on the roof of the shop. Over the years it has remained a local favorite hangout for the residents of the city and soon captured the eyes of tourists driving through. - [2] - Bill Jr. took over the business and expanded the shop to keep up with the demand of locals and tourists. Northshore Creamery was even selected as a top-ten shop to visit by Travel & Tour Magazine.
In 1988, Northshore Creamery was featured in the hit Hollywood movie Future Then and Now, which made it the top ice cream shop to visit by out-of-towners and tourists. - [3] - Efforts were made by various corporations to buy the business from the Bradley family, but Bill Jr. and his son William insisted on keeping the business within the family, which pleased the residents of Northshore. - [4] - "We're keeping things small in scale and we're slowly expanding", explained William. "In order to keep the quality of our ice cream fresh andjust the way my grandfather created his recipes, we don't want to take any short cuts, which is why we need time."

part7.description:
Announcement from Acreton City Council
April 3

Acreton City Council will be creating a new task force charged with reducing unnecessary spending over the next fiscal year, The team of twelve people will be comprised of local business leaders, union representatives, civil servants, and financial consultants. Group members are due to be selected by the end of this month and will begin work almost immediately the following month planning ways to reduce annual local government costs by 10% over the next year by eliminating waste.

Applications for a position are being accepted at this time. Please contact the city council at admin@acretoncc.gov for any Information about getting yourself or your organization involved in the project.

Janet Logan[2:15]I just got off the phone and Mr. King informed me that he wanted his order a couple of weeks earlier than originally planned. Do you think this may be possible?
Margaret Lee[2:16]There's no problem on our end. We have all the fabrics ready and cut into their appropriate shapes and sizes. They are ready for the sewing machines.
Jason Brown[2:17]My team is currently working on the orders from Mr. Bartelli. We have over 1000 units to sew and another order from Carla Bean after that.
Janet Logan[2:18]Mr. Bartelli doesn't need his order until the end of the month and Ms. Bean's orders can wait until next week. I can authorize your team to begin this order first.
Jason Brown[2:19]What is being made and how many units are needed?
Janet Logan[2:20]Long-sleeved men's dress shirts. We need 100 units in small, 300 in medium, 300 in large, and 100 in extra-large.
Jason Brown[2:21]OK then, I think we can finish those in two days.
Peter William[2:22]We can get buttons on all 800 units within 2-4 hours.
Janet Logan[2:23]Thank you so much. I appreciate your help. I'm glad that we can accommodate one of our best clients this way.

part7.description:
Unsworthy Manufacturing
Date: Wednesday, October 17
Subject: Recycling

In response to pressure from local environmental groups, as of November 1 we will be separating all of our industrial waste for recycHng. Collections will be made twice weekly on Tuesdays and Fridays from the regional recycling center, which will be supplying colored receptacles for different kinds of waste. All oils should be placed in the green container. All metals and glass belong in the red one. ATI paper waste should go into the blue one. Plastics will be collected for recyclrng as normal.

As this new policy also carries a financial benefit to the company, managers In all manufacturing bays are responsible for ensuring that the new protocols for waste disposal are followed, and failure to comply with the policy could result in disciplinary action.

Further information about our updated environmental practices will shortly be available on the website. Training sessions for managers will be held on Monday, October 22, but please contact me if you have any further questions in the meantime.

Regards,
Davis Jeeland
Operations Director, Unsworthy Manufacturing

part7.description:
Normanville Farmers' Market
April 9
Dear Normanville Resident,

This year's first Normanville Farmers' Market will be open on Saturday, April 14, on Clark Street, between Main Street and Park Street. The farmers' market will be available between 9:00A.M. and 5s:o00o P.M. The mayor of Normanville, Tom Daley, will be present to deliver an address at the opening ceremony. A lot of local farmers, food vendors, and street performers will be at the venue.

"This vibrant market will give our local farmers a nice place to sell their fresh produce. Additionally, because we cut out some middle processes, our prices are lower than those of average grocery stores," said Suzy Hammer, executive director of the Normanville Farmers' Association.

Ms. Hammer also mentioned that currently there is not enough parking space to accommodate shoppers. The Normanville Farmers' Association plans on expanding parking space in the coming months after the market has opened this Saturday. In the meantime, she advises Normanville residents who will visit the market to use public transportation in order to avoid parking difficulties.

The Normanville Farmers' Market is different from other grocery stores that supplly mass-produced food products. The market will provide organic produce that is full of essential vitamins and minerals. As you know, the market will also help the local economy.

Please come this Saturday and see what the Normanville Farmers' Market has to offer!

Sincerely,
Naormanville Farmers' Association

Parkway City is bracing for another holiday season and urging its citizens and tourists to keep track of their belongings. - [1] - Every year, more than 2000 items show up at the city (ost and found located at Parkway City Hall. "But we get even more lost items during the holiday season," explained Jean King, the managing director of the lost and found, "From around November 25 to January 2, we get a 25% increase in the number of items that are brought to us."
- [2] - Everything from keys, sunglasses, umbrellas, and jewelry to electronic devices, luggage, and shopping bags full of newly purchased items have been brought to the center over the years. "The strangest item we got was a suitcase futl of period piece costumes," says Jean. "The intern working for a film at the time was happy to get it back."

part7.description:
Tech Life Hires New CEO

New York, April 12—'Amid a crisis of low sales and disappointing performance, the technology company Tech Life has hired Steve Cross as its new chief executive officer. Previously, he was the chief financial officer at the technology investment firm Esta Resources in San Francisco, California. He assumed the position of CEO at the company—based in Dallas, Texas just this Monday. Stockholders voted unanimously for the appointment, hoping the new CEO will bring renewed vitality and strength to thecompany.

"Mr. Cross has an impressive record as a business leader who makes smart decisions," commented Lynn Dyer, the director of human resources at Tech Life. "We have faith that he will lead us in a new direction that will help develop new markets and optimize our company operations hi general,"

Steve Cross graduated from Chester University in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, with a master's degree in business administration. He once served as head of the American League of Business Leaders and is a dedicated family man.
To: Steve Cross <scross@techlife.com>
From: Lynn Dyer <ldyer@techlife.com>
Subject: Welcome!
Date: April 15
Dear Mr. Cross,

It has been almost two years since we met. I am so glad to be collaborating with you again after we worked in the same department at Esta Resources. I felt we cooperated very well at that time, and I had been hoping to work with you again. You will find that we have very dedicated and hard-working teams here. If there is anything I can_do to help you make the transition, please don't hesitate to ask.

Additionally, Tech Life has recenttly added five new managers to our company. If you have time, please visit them when they will all be attending a mandatory training session at 3:00 P.M. this afternoon in Room 403.

Sincerely,

Lynn Dyer
Director of Human Resources
Tech Life

The Association of Future and Culture (AFC)
Quarterly Conference
Homer Conference Center, January 10

2:00 P.M.Kelly O'Neill, President, AFC; Principal, Mulligan Elementary School
Welcoming speech
2:30 P.M.Mark Kreskas, CEO, SEM Development Group
Enhancing global awareness: leadership and diversity
3:30 P.M.Lucy Hoover, Co-owner, Piedmont Adult Education Center
Gender and fairness of leadership
4:30 P.M.Jon Kimura, Store Manager, Kent Grocery Store
The foundations of leadership in the workplace
5:30 P.M.Kenneth Schneider, Professor, Brookstone University
Ethics and morality in leadership
6:30 P.M.Question-and-answer session
To: AFC Members <members@futureculture.org>
From: Keylly O'Neill <kellyoneill@futureculture.org>
Date: January 11
Attachment: free_talk.jpg
Subject: Quarterly Conference
Dear AFC Members,

This quarterrlly conference has been another monumental success. I thank all of you for participating and sharing your expertise with others. I hope you can take the skills learned from the conference and apply them in your local of!fices and workpllaces. Additionally, I encourage all of you to consider giving a presentattion at the next conference. If you are interested in doing so, contact Amy Garcia at amygarcia@® futureculture.org.

Iwould also like to inform you of the invitation made by Kenneth Schneider, who will be giving a talk entitled "Gaining confidence through leadership" in his workplace next month. The talk will be free and open to the public. For more information, please see the attached file.

Finally, it came to my attention that some members were not able to attend the conference due to schedulling conflicts. Therefore, from now on all future conferences will be streamed simultaneouslly on our website so that distant members ·can watch and listen.

Sincerely,
Kelly O'Neill,
President

To: Lillian Ross <lillian@goods.com>
From: Eric West <eric@gmail.com>
Date: November 4, 10:34 A.M.
Subject: Website Development
Attachment: Details
Dear Ms. Ross,

You contacted us last week in order to ask some of our computer programmers to help your company develop a website. JM Solutions would be happy to offer you our services.

As I said on the phone, we will help design and program a website that will attract more customers and offer an online sales platform. During this time, we will need to hold meetings with your marketing division in order to best capture your company's goals. Once the website has been completed in mid-February next year, we will hold a training seminar in order to train your employees in the skills necessary to maintain and update your website. The website development and training seminar will cost a total of $32,000. We request that a deposit of 10% be paid in advance. Please see the attached file for detailed costs and schedules.

We look forward to working with you in the near future. Our staff members will strive to meet all your needs. Therefore, just let me know when your marketing division is available to meet us in person and discuss some of the details of the project. Please contact me at your convenience.

Eric West
To: Lillian Ross <lillian@goods.com>
From: Raymond Wells <raymond@gmail.com>Date: Novemeber 4, 10:37 A.M.
Subject: First Quater Budget
Attachment: Q1_Budget
Dear Ms. Ross,

I have attached tthie current draft for the company's budget for the first quarter of next year. As you will notice, all of the profits made from this year's back-to-school sale are planned to be spent on billboard advertisements on the main highways. I will call a design team later this afternoon and ask them to create eye-catching images for the advertisement.

At our last meeting, you mentioned that you would like to review the budget before it is finalized. I have already included employee raises in the first quarter's expenses, but if you can think of anything else, please let me know. I would like to have the budget finalized before next week's planning meeting.

Raymond Wells
To: Raymond Wells <raymond@gmail.com>
From: <lillian@goods.com>
Date: November 4, 10:40 AM
Subject: Emergency Budget Addition
Dear Mr. Wells,

I1 am glad you forwarded me your proposed budget when you did. Just prior to receiving your e-mail, I received an estimate for our planned website development. It looks like it is going to be more expensive than I had anticipated. Altthough the final bill of $32,000 is not due immediately, we will have to find an extra $3,200 in next year's first quarter budget if we want to proceed with JM Solutions' proposal.

If you have any questions regarding this matter, please just come to my office and we can go over where we can make the tough cuts to come up with this funding.
